card.name: Adjectives in old historical prose
card.fires_on: Words in the middle of a phrase in old-fashioned historical or religious prose, such as an adjective (trivial, principal, great, constant) or a linking word (with, of, and) before a noun. The setting is 19th-century style writing about history, missions or druids.

modes.label: Adjective before noun
modes.description: An emphatic adjective that comes just before a noun in a historical narrative.
modes.example: it is indeed touching to see how eagerly they grasp at the most<< trivial>> things which could be thus construed.

modes.label: Linking word in a phrase
modes.description: A small word such as with, of, the or and in the middle of a phrase in a scholarly passage.
